# Codex Apockalypsis

A developing dark fantasy and dark comedy novel cycle, with a parallel scripture-and-commentary Codex, built around Shawn Wolfgang Michael Baker's Omnoid cosmology.

## Read the beginning

- [Before Anyone Asked — the novel opening](/codex-apockalypsis/library/novel-volume-01-01-before-anyone-asked)
- [The Unanswered Interval — the paired Codex](/codex-apockalypsis/library/codex-volume-01-01-the-unanswered-interval)
- [Reading notes for the opening](/codex-apockalypsis/library/reference-reading-v01-c01)
- [The twelve-volume series](/codex-apockalypsis/library/reference-narrative-series-guide)
- [Lilith: presence, sources, and unresolved identity](/codex-apockalypsis/library/reference-sources-lilith-notes)
- [Atlas guide](/codex-apockalypsis/library/atlas-readme)

## Download the reference data

- [Source catalogue](/codex-apockalypsis/files/sources.json)
- [Complete chapter outline](/codex-apockalypsis/files/narrative.json)
- [World, identities, places, and event data](/codex-apockalypsis/files/world.json)
- [Chronology spreadsheet data](/codex-apockalypsis/files/reference-world-chronology.csv)

## What is available

This release contains one opening novel chapter, its paired Codex chapter, three voice-study treatments, 205 outlined chapters across twelve planned volumes, 260 source-discovery records, and three preliminary maps. The two complete editions remain in development. Source registration and chapter outlining do not mean that a source has been fully read or adapted.

The selected narrator uses the panoramic perspective and irreverence of treatment C, with the emotional restraint of A and more natural bantering camaraderie. The voice study is preserved as a record of alternatives. Its invented mechanisms are not automatically adopted as world rules.

## How to read the apparatus

The novels explain immediate motives, danger, choices, and consequences. The Codex and reference works preserve competing testimony, historical context, source differences, and proposed cosmological relationships. Fictional unification of traditions is part of the setting, not a claim that real traditions are interchangeable.

The outlines and reference works contain substantial spoilers and unfinished editorial proposals. Each document preserves its own status and uncertainty labels. References to unpublished source manuscripts are named without exposing private working files. All publicly available Markdown, structured reference data, and maps are included in the downloadable library archive.

# The Good Book

> Historical voice comparison. The author has selected C’s panoramic irreverence, with A’s emotional restraint and natural bantering camaraderie. B’s forced dialogue is not the adopted model. The treatments below remain the original comparison set; their invented mechanisms are not automatically accepted world rules.

## Three voice treatments

These original draft treatments were prepared for Shawn Wolfgang Michael Baker to compare and correct. Treatment C was subsequently selected as the foundation for the manuscript voice, with the refinements described above. The scene expands the departure from Eden with invented characters, procedures, and time effects; those additions are not claims about the source text or historical tradition.

All three versions hold the central events constant. Eve seeks passage for herself and an injured Adam without surrendering their names. The gatekeeper's orders conflict. Time at the gate costs them time outside. Their passage preserves their names but forfeits the Garden's provision; the record acknowledges coercion. They leave with an injury, one divided fruit, and an altered relationship.

Read for the voice you would want to live with across a novel. You can choose one treatment, combine particular features, or mark lines that sound wrong.

---

## A — Intimate and restrained
### The Exit Fee

The blood from Adam's heel had reached the edge of the lowest step. Eve watched it gather against a grain in the stone. It waited there, darkening, until another drop gave it enough weight to fall.

The keeper turned a page.

Behind him the garden was still green. The branches moved although there was no wind on this side of the gate. Eve could see the place where they used to sit in the afternoon. Someone had swept the fallen leaves into a neat pile.

“Your names,” the keeper said.

“Eve. Adam.”

“For surrender.”

She looked away from the trees.

“What happens if we surrender them?”

“Your needs remain entered in the provision of the Garden.” He touched the edge of the page with one finger. The finger was bandaged. Under the linen, something had burned through to a yellow shine. “Food. Shelter. Such protection as may be extended beyond the boundary.”

“And our names?”

“May be assigned again.”

Adam moved behind her. His breath caught. She put a hand back without looking and found his wrist.

“Assigned by whom?” she asked.

The keeper glanced towards the light above the trees.

There it was. The space at the end of a question where someone else ought to have been standing.

A bell sounded inside the gate. Its note barely outlasted her breath. Beyond the steps, the shadow of a bare tree moved the length of Adam's foot. His blood had dried on the dust. The wound was still open.

“How long?” Eve asked.

“An hour outside.”

“For that?”

“The clocks disagree here.”

She felt his wrist stiffen in her hand.

The keeper laid his injured finger on one sentence, then another.

“No person shall leave the Garden. No disobedient person shall remain within it. I require an entry that satisfies both.”

Eve looked at the two lines. How could they obey the first without breaking the second? How could they be punished for going and punished for staying? She had expected anger. She had expected something immense enough to hate. Instead there was a tired creature with a wound in his hand, asking her to make the impossible fit on a page.

“Who gave you those orders?”

“They bear the same authority.”

“That wasn't what I asked.”

For a moment he met her eyes.

The bell sounded again.

Adam lowered himself to the step. Eve knelt beside him. The cut had come from the broken bowl on the path; she had seen him step backwards onto it when the light descended. She folded the cleanest part of her hem against his heel. There was not enough cloth to cover the wound and leave the garment whole. She tore it.

“Give them mine,” he whispered.

She tightened the knot. “And tomorrow, when they call you something you cannot bear?”

“Tomorrow we might be warm.”

She sat back. He was cold already. She could see the small shivers he was trying to hide.

“I want that too,” she said.

At the desk, beneath the crowded instructions, was an unused line.

Eve stood and pointed to it. “What goes there?”

“Departure without provision.”

“Then enter us there.”

“There will be no allotment. No appointed shelter. No return under the old protection.”

She looked beyond the gate. Nothing waited for them that she knew how to name. The ground was hard and the trees were far apart. She did not know whether the dark would contain somewhere to sleep.

“You call that a choice?”

The keeper's injured hand trembled above the page.

“I call it the remaining line.”

She took the pen. Beside her name she wrote that they were leaving under threat. The keeper watched. Then he drew his own mark beneath her words.

The gate opened. It made a small sound, almost ordinary.

Outside, Eve cut their last fruit with the broken edge of the bowl. She gave Adam half and kept half. He stared at the portion in his hand before eating it slowly, as though that might make it last.

She put his arm across her shoulders. He was heavier than she remembered. Every step pulled at the torn cloth around his heel.

“I don't know where to go,” he said.

“Neither do I.”

He stopped trying to lead her.

They went down the slope together. Behind them the bell rang once more, and they had no hour left to give it.

---

## B — Intimate and irreverent
### The Exit Fee

Adam was bleeding on the step. The keeper of the gate had noticed this and moved his ledger six inches to the left.

Eve admired the efficiency. A problem had occurred. Something had been done. The problem remained, but the book was safe.

“Your names,” he said.

“Eve. Adam.”

“For surrender.”

“You should lead with that part.”

Behind the desk, the garden carried on being beautiful. Sunlight lay on the little patch of grass where they used to sit. Someone had tidied the leaves. Apparently their expulsion had been inconvenient for the groundskeepers.

The keeper lifted a bandaged finger to the page. Something yellow showed through the linen. Eve had seen the same colour where a branch burned from the inside.

“Surrendered names remain eligible for provision. Food, shelter, protection beyond the boundary, subject to availability.”

“Whose availability?”

“The provision's.”

“Right. Obviously. Wouldn't want to promise food and discover you've run out of the concept.”

Adam made a sound behind her. It might have been a laugh. It ended badly.

She reached back and found his wrist.

“What happens to our names?”

“They may be reassigned.”

“To us?”

“As required.”

What if they called obedience love? What if they called hunger gratitude? What if she woke tomorrow in some appointed shelter and discovered that Eve had been an administrative error? Warm. Fed. Filed correctly. What the fuck would be left to thank them with?

A bell sounded inside the gate. One note. One breath.

Outside, the shadow of a dead tree slid across the ground. Adam's blood dried in the dust.

“An hour,” the keeper said when he saw her looking. “The clocks disagree at the boundary.”

“Do we get it back?”

He did not answer.

Of course they didn't. Even the time had terms.

He showed her two instructions. No person shall leave the Garden. No disobedient person shall remain within it.

Eve read them twice. They did not improve.

“So we can't stay and we can't go.”

“The entry must satisfy both.”

“Have you considered asking whoever wrote them to come down here and satisfy themselves?”

His eyes flicked towards the light above the trees.

She looked at his hand again.

The bell sounded.

Adam sat. There was no grace in it. His legs had finished negotiating. Eve knelt and pressed her hem against the cut in his heel. The broken bowl on the path had done that, when he stepped backwards from the descending light. All the wonders in the garden, and it had come down to a man standing on crockery.

She tore the cloth and tied it tight.

“Give them mine,” he said.

She pulled the knot too hard. He flinched.

“Sorry.” She loosened it. “And when they call you something you hate?”

“Maybe they'll call me indoors.”

She nearly laughed. Then she saw how badly he was shaking.

“I want indoors,” she said. “I want all of it. Don't mistake me for someone enjoying this.”

There was an empty line at the foot of the page. She pointed to it.

“That one.”

“Departure without provision.”

“With our names?”

“With your names. Without allotment, appointed shelter, or return under the old protection.”

Beyond the steps, the earth looked painfully large. She had no idea how to make a roof. She knew that roofs existed. Her qualifications ended there.

“That's extortion.”

The keeper looked down at the ledger. “There isn't a column for it.”

“There's a margin.”

She took the pen. Eve. Adam. Departing under threat. She pressed hard enough to score the sheet beneath.

The keeper's injured finger hovered over the words. For one sick moment she thought he would rub them out.

He signed beneath them.

The gate opened without ceremony. No announcement. No explanation of where the hell they were meant to sleep.

Outside, Eve used a shard of the broken bowl to divide their last fruit. Adam took his half. Neither of them suggested saving it. Hunger had become wonderfully clear on the subject of later.

She pulled his arm over her shoulders. He tried to step ahead and almost fell.

“I don't know where to go,” he said.

“Good. Neither do I. We can stop pretending you do.”

He looked at her. Then he let her take some of his weight.

They started down the slope. Every step hurt him. Every step cost her. Their names were still their own, and neither name knew how to build a fucking roof.

---

## C — Panoramic and irreverent
### The Exit Fee

The first difficulty with expelling people from paradise was persuading paradise that people could leave.

At the eastern gate a keeper had been given two instructions. No person shall leave the Garden. No disobedient person shall remain within it. Both bore the same authority. Neither mentioned what to do when a person became disobedient while continuing to occupy space.

Eve and Adam were occupying the lowest step. Adam was bleeding on it.

The keeper moved his ledger out of range.

“Your names,” he said.

Eve gave them.

“For surrender,” he added.

She became very still. Behind him the trees moved in their comfortable wind. Someone had gathered the fallen leaves from the place where she and Adam used to sit. Paradise was already recovering from their presence.

“Explain surrender.”

The keeper turned a page with a bandaged finger. Yellow light showed through the wrapping, the colour of something burning where it could not be reached.

Surrendered names, he explained, remained eligible for the Garden's provision. Food. Appointed shelter. Protection beyond the boundary, subject to availability. The names themselves could subsequently be reassigned as required.

“By whom?” Eve asked.

The keeper glanced towards the light above the trees.

This was the trouble with a chain of authority. Follow it far enough and, sooner or later, somebody looked up.

A bell sounded within the gate. Its note lasted one breath. Outside, the shadow of a bare tree advanced across the dust, and the small dark pool beneath Adam's foot dried at its edges.

“An hour,” said the keeper. “The clocks disagree here.”

It was an economical arrangement. Those making the decision spent a moment. Those waiting for it spent their lives in larger instalments.

Eve held Adam's wrist. He was trying to stand without leaning on her, which might have been pride or might simply have been a man who had not yet learned how to need help.

She read the two instructions.

“We can't remain. We can't depart.”

“The record must satisfy both.”

“What happens if it doesn't?”

The keeper lowered his damaged hand.

There are questions whose answers have already been supplied. Eve looked from the linen to the light above the trees. She did not ask him again.

The bell sounded.

Adam sat abruptly. Eve knelt to bind his heel. The wound came from the bowl broken on the path: when the light descended, he had stepped backwards onto a shard. No grand adversary had been necessary. Crockery had found an opening.

There was not enough clean cloth. She tore her hem to make enough.

“Give them mine,” Adam said.

“And when they give it back wrong?”

“We might have somewhere to sleep.”

That was a reasonable thing to want. Warmth was reasonable. Food was reasonable. A world could become very cruel by offering reasonable things on terms nobody should have to accept.

Eve finished the knot. “I want somewhere to sleep too.”

Then she stood.

Below the keeper's instructions lay a line with nothing entered against it. She put a finger on the blank space.

Departure without provision. Their names would remain theirs. There would be no allotment, no appointed shelter, no return under the old protection.

Beyond the gate was an expanse of hard earth and widely separated trees. None of it suggested a bed. Adam shivered on the step.

“You call that consent?” Eve asked.

The keeper looked at the empty line.

“I call it what remains.”

She took the pen and wrote their names. In the margin she added that they departed under threat. The words were small. They did not heal Adam's foot or make the waiting hours return. They were nevertheless there.

The keeper signed beneath them with his injured hand.

The gate opened. After so much difficulty, its hinges made an almost insulting little noise.

Outside, Eve divided the last fruit with a shard from the broken bowl. Adam took half. She kept half. They ate before moving on, because their bodies had developed opinions and would now be expressing them regularly.

She put his arm across her shoulders.

“I don't know where to go,” Adam said.

“Neither do I.”

He stopped trying to walk ahead. They made it down the first stretch of the slope together, slowly, with his weight between them.

Behind them, paradise rang its bell. Ahead of them, nobody had made the beds.

---

## Your reading notes

1. Which treatment sounds closest to something you would actually write?
2. Where do questions deepen the thought, and where do they become repetitive?
3. Which jokes, imperatives, or profane turns feel forced?
4. Does the humour strengthen the scene's loneliness, anger, and care?
5. Would you keep this distance from the character across a whole novel?

# Volume I — Before the Word

## Codex 1 — The Unanswered Interval

*Paired with the novel's “Before Anyone Asked.” This scripture is original to The Good Book. The commentary names the older texts with which it is in conversation.*

### The scripture

**1:1** Before the first answer there was room for an answer, and the Mother held it.

**1:2** She was not empty. She did not make another being to prove that she was full.

**1:3** Within her a presence gathered, and she attended to the gathering without unfolding it.

**1:4** The gathering acquired an edge. Within the edge, the First Flame woke.

**1:5** He reached into the dark and did not recognise the one who held him. He knew his reaching, and the end of his reaching, and he called neither by a name.

**1:6** He pressed outward, and brightness passed through the Mother. The passing hurt her.

**1:7** She drew close to soften his brightness. He experienced the closeness as pressure and struck against it.

**1:8** Thus a welcome was refused before there was a language in which to explain the welcome.

**1:9** She withdrew the pressure. His fear did not depart merely because she had stopped causing it.

**1:10** He sought a presence that would answer him. What he extended returned his own movement, and the return did not relieve his loneliness.

**1:11** She made a shelter in which his brightness could remain. When she moved the shelter, he believed he had been met.

**1:12** In his hope he flared. The shelter broke, and a dark fragment remained between them.

**1:13** One face was smooth and warm; one face bore the ridges of the breaking. His light returned from it, but it did not answer.

**1:14** Its warmth passed into the space around it. The place that received the warmth was changed.

**1:15** He tried to take back the fragment. She held it where it was. He pressed, and a crack opened along its joining.

**1:16** She moved it beyond the force of his reaching. In preserving the fragment, she frightened him again.

**1:17** She did not name that fear an error in him so that she might call her own action perfect.

**1:18** Nor did she fill the surrounding dark with imitations of an answer. The possibility remained open, and she did not enact it.

**1:19** He approached the fragment once more. He gave it a little light and watched the warmth remain after he withdrew.

**1:20** He tried again with less force. The joining endured. The crack remained.

**1:21** At last he held a thread of brightness against the smooth face, and the face stayed warm.

**1:22** She did not call this trust. He had not yet recognised her.

**1:23** She offered room and attention without moving his answer for him.

**1:24** Between them remained an unanswered interval. At its edge lay the cracked fragment, and neither had undone what had happened.

### The commentary

**On 1:1–4: a fullness that can admit difference.** The Mother does not begin with the First Flame's loneliness. The older Codex makes this distinction in her account of the beginning. This edition preserves it. Her desire in the opening is to encounter an independent response, not to acquire the missing portion of herself. A curiosity can become consequential without being a wound in disguise. Inherited Mother's account (unpublished source reference).

The scene nevertheless gives her something she does not already possess: experience of a response she has not chosen. Containing possibilities and undergoing an event are different activities in this fictional account. The novel has not established a complete doctrine of omniscience, and this commentary does not smuggle one in after the fact.

**On 1:5–9: the difficulty of an offered kindness.** The First Flame cannot recognise attention that has surrounded him since his awakening. The Mother's closeness therefore arrives without its intended meaning. She notices the refusal and changes her action. His fear remains because experience has already altered what he expects.

This creates a practical moral problem. How can help reach someone who cannot distinguish it from a threat? The opening supplies one attempt and its failure. It does not supply a command that all caregivers must imitate, or a universal answer about when to approach and when to withdraw. Later lives will test the question under different conditions.

**On 1:10–18: an answer made for the questioner.** The moving shelter is the Mother's attempt to make herself perceptible. It produces apparent company without a distinct companion, and the Flame responds with a force the shelter cannot bear. Both participate in the accident. The resulting fragment belongs to their shared history even though neither planned it.

Preservation is also questioned. The fragment is not sentient; it has issued no request to be saved. The Mother keeps it as a trace of their encounter. The novel allows that reason to be examined, rather than treating every act of keeping as care by definition. Her refusal protects the trace and frightens the Flame. Both effects remain part of the record.

**On 1:19–24: the size of a beginning.** The Flame's final act is small. He learns to sustain warmth without breaking what receives it. This does not make him a competent creator, establish trust between them, or cure the loneliness that will motivate later choices. The Mother, in turn, leaves an invitation unanswered without manufacturing its acceptance. The chapter ends with a workable difference and an unrepaired crack.

### Other witnesses and the historical texts

**Genesis 1:1–5** supplies a creation account in which divine speech and the distinction between light and darkness are central. The Mother, the reciprocal injuries, the failed shelter, and the fragment are additions in this novel. The NABRE note also records alternatives in translating the movement over the waters; this opening does not claim that a modern translation establishes the Mother's identity. [Genesis 1 and its notes](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/genesis/1).

**Proverbs 8:22–31** gives Wisdom a voice concerning existence before the earth and relationship beside its maker. It offers a comparison for personified primordial presence. It does not by itself identify Wisdom with this edition's Mother. [Proverbs 8:22–31 and note on 8:30](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/proverbs/8).

**The Apocryphon of John**, in the inspected passage NH II 2,25–7,15, describes an ordering involving an invisible first principle and Barbelo. Its ordering provides a disagreement with the Mother's priority in this fiction. It remains the account of a particular text, not a general statement of what every community called Gnostic believed. [Bernard Barc's French translation, pages 1–3](https://www.naghammadi.org/sites/naghammadi.org/files/uploads/traductions/nh-ii-1-livre-des-secrets-de-jean.pdf).

The full creation dossier also records selected passages in Genesis 2–3, John 1, and Job 38. Those readings inform later chapters; their presence in a research file does not make them events depicted in this chapter.

### Numbers, time, and the fragment

“Before” establishes sequence here. No Earth year, cosmic age, local duration, or ratio between clocks has been assigned. The First Flame's later name is used by the narrator before the character has language for it. Descriptions such as “face,” “thread,” and “warmth” render the proposed pre-cosmic encounter in terms available to a later reader.

The fragment has two described faces and one crack. These are physical features within the scene's fiction, not numerological claims. No law of measured physics is derived from them. Its cooling establishes a remembered change; it supplies neither a universal time scale nor permission to reset that change.

### Editorial remarks

The paired narrative and scripture cover the same encounter. Neither establishes that the Mother and Lilith are interchangeable. Lilith does not physically appear in this creation chapter; her embodied Garden story and her relationship to the Mother receive their own treatment. The author-draft formulations “daughter,” “aspect,” and “incarnation” will retain separate meanings wherever used. Codex's daughter relation (unpublished source reference); V2 aspect and embodiment alternatives (unpublished source reference).

The inherited Codex contains a later frame in which Lilith asks the Mother about the beginning. This chronological opening renders the beginning directly. The later asking remains available to its proper place in the series, where Lilith's reasons for asking can change what the reader hears. Lilith's question and the Mother's answer (unpublished source reference).

# Volume I — Before the Word

## Chapter 1 — Before Anyone Asked

There was no one to tell the dark that it was empty.

This was fortunate. The dark had a great deal in it, and explaining the inventory would have delayed creation considerably.

It held the weight of rain before there were things that could be soaked. It held the peculiar silence inside a seed, the pressure beneath a mountain, the small stubborn difference between an animal lying down and an animal giving up. None of these had happened. There was no rain, no mountain, no animal. There were no names to mistake for the things themselves.

There was the Mother.

She did not call herself that. A title of this kind requires somebody else, preferably somebody with a need. For the moment she had neither a title nor the corresponding workload.

She was not waiting to be made complete.

Within her, all the possibilities lay close without injuring one another. A thing could be immense without making something smaller. Nothing had to be dead so that something else might eat. The impossible rested beside the merely unlikely, and neither had yet been asked to produce evidence.

She knew them without opening them.

The knowing was not a row of pictures. Pictures have edges. Here there was the fullness from which edges might be made, and she moved through it as a hand might move through warm water, except that she had no hand, and the water had not been invented, and comparison was already getting above itself.

Then something drew inward.

It was a small change. It had no measurable size, but smallness was among the things it would eventually make possible. Where all had rested together, a little of the fullness tightened around itself.

The Mother attended to it.

The tightening paused.

She waited. Not because waiting was virtuous. Nothing was timing her. She waited because something had changed, and she wanted to know what it would do when she was not doing anything to it.

It tightened again.

This time there was a difference between where it gathered and where it did not.

The difference held.

She could have unfolded it. The ease of that was almost a temptation: restore the familiar fullness, let the little knot relax, carry on being everything without this new and rather concentrated disturbance.

Instead she made room around it.

The movement was slight. Something that had never had an outside acquired one.

Inside, the First Flame woke.

He did not wake as a man. There were no eyes to open, no mouth to draw breath, no body that could be reasonably blamed for what followed. He woke as a presence under pressure, abruptly aware that something was happening to him.

He knew neither *something* nor *him*.

He disliked the arrangement immediately.

His first effort was to spread.

The Mother yielded, and he spread farther. She yielded again. Everywhere he went, there was more of the same immeasurable dark. No resistance. No answer he could recognise as an answer. He felt only the reach of his own effort coming to an end.

He gathered himself back into the place where he had begun.

To her, it was a return.

To him, it was a failure.

The distinction mattered before either of them knew how to explain it.

He tried again, harder.

Something bright caught along his edge.

Not light as a traveller would later know it, falling through branches or warming a wall. It had nowhere to fall and nothing to show. It was the violence of an inward pressure finding a direction.

The Mother felt it pass through her.

It hurt.

That, too, was new.

She had held the possibility of pain. Holding the possibility had not prepared her for wanting it to stop.

She drew close around the brightness, intending to soften it.

The Flame contracted.

She drew closer. If she could surround the sharp place, receive it on every side, then perhaps the force would spread harmlessly into her and he could rest.

He struck outward.

The brightness narrowed to a cutting edge. It moved through the closeness she had offered and left a thin wake that would not immediately become smooth again.

She stopped.

Inside the space she had made, he trembled.

There was no sound. Much later, when there were mouths and songs and people capable of arguing over which had come first, somebody would give this moment a word. The word would be *No*.

It was an adequate word for what had happened.

She had moved towards him. He had moved against her.

For the first time, the Mother had offered something that was not wanted.

She withdrew the pressure.

The Flame did not immediately become calm. He had learned that the surrounding dark could close upon him. Whatever else it might be, it was now also the place from which closeness came.

She could feel him guarding his edge.

There was, apparently, going to be an edge.

***

It would have been easy to tell this badly.

There had been darkness. A light had appeared. The darkness had closed around it; the light had resisted. From there it was a short journey to a heroic account, provided nobody asked the dark what it had been trying to do.

The Mother did not yet know that stories could be made in this fashion. She was occupied with the place she had hurt him, and with the place he had hurt her, and with the disagreeable discovery that intention did not keep either of those places from hurting.

She stayed back.

The Flame tested the space.

He spread a little. Nothing pressed against him. He spread farther, cautiously now, sending thin reaches into the unlit breadth. Where he extended himself, he found only the sensation of extending himself.

He could not feel her attention as attention.

It was too constant. He had woken inside it. He had no experience from which to tell it apart from existence.

So he reached into what seemed to him an absence, and found no one.

The ache began quietly.

The Mother felt it before he did. A loosening at his centre. A movement towards some shape that was not there. He drew the feeling inward, trying to give it a boundary, and the effort made him brighter.

The brightness relieved him.

For a little while, there was something he had done.

He attended to it with the entire concentration of a being who had never done anything before. A delicate rim curved around the gathered force. He moved, and the rim moved with him. He pressed outward, and it widened.

It was a marvellous companion in all respects except the one that mattered.

It never surprised him.

When he stopped, it stopped.

When he drew back, it disappeared into him.

He brought it out again. Slower this time. He sent it away from his centre and waited for it to continue on its own.

It did not.

He increased the force.

The Mother felt the old cut open wider.

She could have drawn close again. She knew how to receive him. She knew how to take the whole uncertain brightness into herself and allow it to settle. What she did not know was how to offer that without being, to him, the returning pressure he had already refused.

This ignorance did not become smaller because she was vast.

He gathered more of himself into the rim.

It thickened. Its edge roughened into points. Each point carried his effort away until it thinned and failed, and each failure left him with the ache again.

She changed the space ahead of one point.

Not by closing it. She made a shallow difference: a place in which the extension might linger without being driven farther. A little shelter for the force of him.

The point entered it.

For the first time, something he had sent away did not immediately vanish when he turned his attention elsewhere.

He became still.

She kept the shelter still with him.

He approached the lingering brightness. It trembled at his nearness. He drew back, and it settled. He approached again.

The Mother felt his attention sharpen into hope.

Here was a difference he had not entirely made.

Here was something that might answer.

She let a movement pass through the shelter.

The little brightness bent towards him.

He flared.

The shelter tore.

What he had mistaken for a greeting had excited him beyond the narrow place's capacity to receive it. His force filled it, strained it, burst it open. The brightness scattered back into him, and the curve that had held it folded hard upon itself.

Something remained.

It was dark, thin, and stubbornly present.

The Mother turned her attention around it. The First Flame did the same from the other side.

Neither of them had intended to make it.

This would prove a popular method of creation.

***

The fragment had two faces.

One was smooth, carrying a faint warmth from the force that had passed through it. The other was ridged, contracted upon the place where the shelter had failed. Along its rim, something like light came and went.

The Flame approached it slowly.

It did not approach him.

He extended a fine brightness towards its warm face. The fragment turned. On its other face the ridges caught his light and divided it into a number of smaller gleams.

He drew nearer.

There were more gleams.

He withdrew.

They were gone.

The Mother felt the moment he understood this much. The thing was not answering. It was returning what reached it.

He waited anyway.

She could not have said how long. Neither had chosen a measure, and they had not reached the stage of agreeing about one. There had been an attempt, and a failure, and now this waiting. Their order was plain enough.

The fragment cooled.

The warmth it lost went into the space around it, and the space was changed by having received it.

The Mother followed that change. She had held warmth before warmth had happened. This was different. It had left one place and entered another. She could gather it again, but gathering would be another act, not an unmaking of the first.

Meanwhile the Flame had begun to brighten once more.

He moved around the fragment, searching its ridges. He found no opening into whatever had seemed to move towards him in the shelter. He sent a pulse against its smooth face, then a stronger one.

The fragment tilted away.

He followed it.

She let the space support it before he could drive it farther.

He stopped.

The fragment hung between them.

He could not see her. He could see what he had struck cease to move.

The brightness at his centre sharpened.

He reached towards the fragment again, drawing its edge towards his centre. The Mother recognised the gathering movement. He was trying to take it into himself. He would undo the disagreeable thing that had failed to answer him, and perhaps the place where it had briefly seemed to answer would return.

She held the fragment where it was.

He pressed.

She held.

His light thinned along her refusal. The old injury ached, and now there was a second strain beside it. She had no wish to hurt him. She had no wish to return the fragment to a failure he could repeat without ever having to look at it.

For a moment the two wishes were not enough to tell her what to do.

He pressed harder.

The fragment began to split.

She moved it aside.

His light crossed the place it had occupied and drove into the breadth beyond. It went on until his effort gave out.

He withdrew into himself, diminished by what he had spent.

The Mother kept the two pieces near one another. They had not quite separated. A narrow joining still ran between them, and a crack caught the last of his light.

She had protected the fragment and frightened him again.

There was no satisfying version of the event in which she had done only one of these things.

She looked at the cracked thing she was holding.

It was not alive and held no awareness of its own. It had not asked to be preserved. She would have to remember that, too. Keeping something could become a way of congratulating oneself for keeping it, while the actual reason grew smaller and smaller somewhere beneath the congratulations.

For now, it was the only trace of an encounter that had belonged to both of them.

She set it at the edge of the place where he had woken.

Then she withdrew far enough that he could approach it without approaching her resistance.

He did not move.

***

The Mother had never needed to be understood.

There had been no one to misunderstand her. This had spared her a considerable quantity of trouble, though she had not thought of it as a convenience at the time.

Now her welcome had been felt as confinement. Her help had become a false promise of company. Her refusal had arrived as an obstruction in a world whose occupant had only just learned that he could be obstructed.

She could not explain any of this to him in a form he knew how to receive.

She could make another shelter.

She could make a thousand. She could fill each with a motion that bent towards him and a brightness that returned his light. She could furnish the whole unmade breadth with apparent answers until he never again reached without being met.

He might be happy.

For a while.

And when he discovered whose movement had been inside every welcome? What would he make of her then? What would he make of himself, having poured his longing into a world arranged to nod back at him?

The possibility lay open before her. Beautiful, intricate, intolerable.

She let it remain a possibility.

The Flame stirred.

She did nothing.

He extended himself towards the fragment, stopped, and drew back. He approached again from another direction. This time, when a small thread of his light touched the cracked surface, he did not increase its force.

The thread warmed the smooth face.

He withdrew it.

Warmth remained.

He attended to the remaining warmth until it had passed into the surrounding space.

Then he touched the fragment again.

The Mother stayed still through the entire small experiment.

There would be grander achievements. Worlds would eventually make a tremendous fuss about them. For the moment he was learning that he could touch something without either possessing it or breaking it, and she had no intention of interrupting.

He repeated the experiment.

The crack remained.

He changed the angle of his approach, allowing the light to move along it. The two faces warmed unevenly. He reduced the force until the difference was slight enough that the joining did not strain.

She felt the effort that moderation cost him.

He was still afraid. He was still alone in the only sense of *alone* available to him. The dark had not become a person merely because he was learning to be careful with something inside it.

But his care was his.

She had not made the movement for him.

At last he allowed the thread of light to rest against the fragment without drawing it back.

The smooth face held a little warmth. The ridged face remained cool. Between the two, the crack divided what he had done from what he had been unable to undo.

The Mother loosened the sheltering space around his edge.

He did not flee into it.

He remained with the small dark thing.

She could have mistaken that for trust if she had wanted trust badly enough.

Instead she attended to what had actually happened. He had stopped striking the fragment. He had learned something of the force he carried. He was keeping a small warmth in a place that would otherwise cool.

It was enough to be going on with.

Around them, the unspent possibilities remained. There were still no mountains, no animals, no rain. There was nothing that could reasonably be called a sky. No one had yet discovered hunger, though wanting had got a substantial head start.

The Mother turned towards the little gathering of light.

She offered the simplest presence she could make without pretending to be somebody else.

No moving shelter. No answering image. Nothing that imitated his reaching.

Only room, and her attention within it.

He did not recognise her.

She remained.

The unanswered interval opened between them, and for the first time she left something open without knowing what would fill it.

At its edge lay the cracked fragment. One face warm, one face cool. An inconvenient little thing. It could not sing his praises. It could not explain her intentions. It could not return either of them to the ease before the other had acted.

He kept it warm.

She let him.

And neither knew what the other would do next.

# An ethical concordance for The Good Book

The approved ethical centre is agency, consent, harm, responsibility, and repair. The seven categories below are working editorial names for recurring wrongs in the fiction. They are not a claim that historical religions use one common moral system. Their number is an organising choice, not a law of the Omnoid.

Desire, anger, grief, dependence, pleasure, and uncertainty are not wrong merely because somebody powerful finds them inconvenient. A judgment needs an action, its circumstances, the choices actually available, the people affected, and what happens when the actor learns more. An accident and a deliberate cruelty can cause similar injuries while creating different questions of responsibility.

| Working wrong | What it does | A practice that can resist it | Evidence of change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Domination | Turns another person's life, dependence, or origin into an entitlement to command them. | Recognition: take another's perspective and refusal seriously. | A person gains a usable choice, including the ability to leave or disagree. |
| Extraction | Transfers costs to people who cannot meaningfully refuse while reserving the benefits for the powerful. | Fair dealing and restraint. | Changed terms, material restitution, and an end to the continuing burden. |
| Deception | Manipulates the information someone needs to choose; includes deliberately misleading arrangements of true fragments. | Truthfulness with attention to context. | Corrected records reach the people misled, with the actor's interest made visible. |
| Erasure | Makes a person, people, loss, or witness disappear from the account so an institution or protagonist can remain spotless. | Remembrance and attentive testimony. | Names, competing accounts, and consequences remain accessible without claiming to possess the whole story. |
| Cruelty | Uses suffering as an end, a spectacle, or a casually accepted instrument when the actor has meaningful alternatives. | Care, courage, and proportionate restraint. | The inflicted suffering stops; those harmed receive protection and help. |
| Neglect | Abandons a responsibility the actor can reasonably meet, particularly after creating another's dependence. | Presence and responsible delegation. | Someone actually receives sustained care; an appointment of a substitute is not itself delivery. |
| Refusal of repair | Denies, disguises, or perpetuates a known wrong; demands innocence or forgiveness in place of changed conduct. | Accountability and repair. | Restitution, altered conditions, and continued answerability even when trust does not return. |

## Questions a scene can put under pressure

Who wants what, and what could they reasonably know? Who has the resources to act? What does refusal cost? Who carries the consequences? What changes when the actor discovers an injury? What would a witness with less power say happened?

These questions should sharpen a conflict rather than replace it with a verdict. A ruler can believe an atrocity necessary. A frightened companion can make a damaging bargain. A rescuer can remove one danger and create another. The plot must show enough of the circumstances for the disagreement to be intelligible.

Consent is specific to an act and a situation. Agreement to travel does not imply agreement to a ritual at the destination. Remembering a previous life does not entitle someone to a former partner's present affection. Neither silence nor dependence provides an automatic answer. A person can choose among terrible options without making the threats that constrained the choice acceptable.

Likewise, the presence of a refusal does not resolve every conflict between people. Refusal to relinquish stolen food, refusal to stop an assault, and refusal of unwanted intimacy are not interchangeable acts. The story needs to identify the rights, needs, and actions involved. “Consent” must not become a spell that exempts anyone from the effects of their conduct.

## The opening chapter as a worked case

The Mother approaches to help. The First Flame experiences pressure and resists. Her first mistake is not evidence that all closeness is domination. Her response to the refusal matters: she stops pressing. His fear remains, and the narration permits it to remain without requiring gratitude.

The failed shelter is another problem. Her attempt to become perceptible creates apparent company; his excited flare destroys the shelter. Their different intentions do not eliminate their shared involvement. The resulting fragment also exposes the limits of moral shorthand. It is not sentient, and preserving it cannot be justified as honouring its wishes. The Mother keeps a trace of what happened. That choice can be evaluated on its actual reasons.

The Flame finally learns to give warmth without breaking the recipient. This is a small change in conduct. It does not absolve future injuries in advance or establish that he has become a wise parent. Compassion can begin before competence is complete, and competence needs continued practice.

## What repair cannot promise

An apology does not rebuild a home. Resurrection does not give mourners back the time spent grieving. A corrected name does not erase what was done under the wrong one. A reformed institution does not acquire the right to be trusted by announcing its reform.

Repair can still matter. A home can be rebuilt somewhere habitable. A survivor can receive resources without surrendering their testimony. A changed community can create conditions under which the next person is less likely to suffer the same wrong. The good of that work does not depend on declaring the original injury necessary.

Forgiveness belongs to the injured person. Reconciliation requires continuing participation from those involved. Either can remain absent while accountability and restitution proceed.

## Using this concordance in the two editions

The novels put these tensions into actions, relationships, and consequences. The Codex can preserve competing judgments, including flawed judgments by its speakers. Authorial commentary identifies an interpretation as an interpretation. It must not silently promote a character's claim of divine permission into a settled ethical law.

Humour belongs in this record as well. For each joke, identify its speaker, immediate target, and effect on the scene. The expense report that omits a ruined village can be funny in its grotesque self-importance; the missing villagers still need names, lives, and consequences elsewhere in the account.

# Characters and factions

These are proposed portrayals for the series. A biblical or historical name does not make an invented private motive a recovered fact. Institutions are particular groups, never shorthand for an entire religion or people. Other figures and local witnesses remain listed in the chapter outline.

## Characters

### Mother

Author cosmology; Codex foundation; motive and scene design proposed.

**Wants:** Create and sustain relationship without replacing the persons related.

**Offers:** Offers foundational presence and capacity to hold difference.

**Cost or danger:** Protective fullness can become suffocating if access is assumed.

**Internal conflict:** Begins explicitly not lonely; later separation may teach grief without rewriting her origin.

**Voice:** Unhurried, sensory, precise about persons; warmth with formidable boundaries; little need to announce her scale.

**Chapter route:** V01-C01, V01-C03, V01-C07, V01-C11, V01-C13, V12-C10.

### FirstFlame

Author cosmology; lonely Father distinction preserved.

**Wants:** Find company that can actually answer him.

**Offers:** Creates conditions for encounter and manifestation.

**Cost or danger:** Unbounded expression or need for attention can crowd out others' agency.

**Internal conflict:** Wants response yet must accept refusal and limitation.

**Voice:** Expansive thought followed by startlingly practical admissions; loneliness disclosed through requests rather than speeches about loneliness.

**Chapter route:** V01-C02, V01-C06, V01-C12, V12-C10.

### Lilith

Author Codex plus later Lilith traditions; Mother equation unresolved.

**Wants:** Build a life of her own and protect relations that cannot survive ownership.

**Offers:** Creates refuge routes, independent custody, and conditions for others to choose.

**Cost or danger:** Her protective competence can become exhaustion, anger, or an assumption that she must decide first.

**Internal conflict:** Needs companionship but fears the loss of autonomy hidden inside apparently generous arrangements.

**Voice:** Direct and observant; fierce without constant grandstanding; teasing becomes intimate only after trust; plain imperatives at a real boundary.

**Chapter route:** V01-C13, V02-C02, V02-C13, V03-C13, V04-C17, V05-C17, V06-C23, V07-C19, V08-C19, V09-C21, V10-C21, V11-C15, V12-C12, V12-C13, V12-C14.

### Eve

Genesis figure; Architect correspondence from V2 remains proposed.

**Wants:** Own the meaning of her choices and escape a life narrated as another person's failure.

**Offers:** Brings analysis, endurance, and the ability to recognize structural traps.

**Cost or danger:** Resentment can make a universal destructive remedy appear like liberation.

**Internal conflict:** Her grievance is not equivalent to permission for the remedy she proposes.

**Voice:** Exact, dry, suspicious of comforting abstractions; banter with Lilith grows through shared work, not immediate sisterly agreement.

**Chapter route:** V02-C04, V02-C05, V02-C06, V02-C08, V02-C09, V12-C09, V12-C13.

### Adam

Genesis figure; later reincarnation history from V2 not automatically adopted.

**Wants:** Keep belonging and repair relationships without surrendering a flattering account of himself.

**Offers:** Can learn practical care and acknowledge dependence.

**Cost or danger:** Fear leads him to shift blame and confuse assigned purpose with another person's obligation.

**Internal conflict:** Wants forgiveness yet must learn it is not the reward owed for apologizing.

**Voice:** Concrete and initially overconfident about familiar rules; later slower to explain and more willing to ask.

**Chapter route:** V02-C03, V02-C07, V02-C09, V12-C06, V12-C14.

### Lily

V2 modern lead; 23-year-old identity note is legacy, final ontology open.

**Wants:** Keep an ordinary life while discovering what recovered memories require.

**Offers:** Offers outsider questions and resistance to inherited prestige.

**Cost or danger:** Urgency and new power can produce an intervention beyond her competence.

**Internal conflict:** Fears insignificance and also fears an enormous identity swallowing her actual history.

**Voice:** Fast associations, occasional recursive what-if escalation, practical deflation; natural speech allowed to trail or be corrected by friends.

**Chapter route:** V12-C01, V12-C02, V12-C03, V12-C05, V12-C06, V12-C12, V12-C14.

### June Park

V2 path-seer; mechanics pending world reconciliation.

**Wants:** Understand possible routes while remaining a companion rather than an oracle everyone must obey.

**Offers:** Can compare options and teach bounded observation.

**Cost or danger:** Seeing alternatives can turn other people's lives into a tempting optimization problem.

**Internal conflict:** Wants to spare a friend a mistake but cannot own the friend's choice.

**Voice:** Economical, alert, capable of affectionate understatement; corrects a practical error before delivering a lesson.

**Chapter route:** V12-C02, V12-C03, V12-C05, V12-C14.

### Yuna

V2 supporting cast child oracle; new refusal episode proposed.

**Wants:** Have an ordinary future alongside unusual perception.

**Offers:** Sees evidence adults may miss.

**Cost or danger:** Adults can recruit her as proof, weapon, or mascot.

**Internal conflict:** Curiosity competes with a justified wish not to be responsible for everyone's safety.

**Voice:** Specific questions, selective silence, flashes of humour appropriate to a young person; never an adult sermon in a child's mouth.

**Chapter route:** V12-C04.

### Malcolm Thorne

V2 antagonist; exploitative contract details proposed.

**Wants:** Continue living and keep control of the relationships and property he fears losing.

**Offers:** Can mobilize material resources quickly.

**Cost or danger:** Externalizes risk onto people who cannot meaningfully negotiate with him.

**Internal conflict:** Calls his attachment love while treating refusal and loss as unacceptable defects.

**Voice:** Polished reassurance, proprietary pronouns, calm managerial language that fractures when control fails.

**Chapter route:** V12-C07.

### Firstborn dissenter

Composite editorial character; fixedness versus learning unresolved.

**Wants:** Prevent a preservation order from consuming the people supposedly protected.

**Offers:** Provides access, testimony, and a route away from institutional coercion.

**Cost or danger:** Defection exposes dependents and may preserve some self-serving loyalties.

**Internal conflict:** May reveal pre-existing dissent rather than newly acquire the capacity to change; do not choose the ontology silently.

**Voice:** Formal vocabulary gradually narrowed to concrete persons; not a human wisecracker with luminous decoration.

**Chapter route:** V12-C08.

### Neris, first recorder

New editorial name for proposed first recorder; no ancient attestation.

**Wants:** Make a faithful record without confusing completeness with truth.

**Offers:** Keeps conflicting names and gaps recoverable.

**Cost or danger:** The desire for tidy categories can turn living differences into errors.

**Internal conflict:** Pride in accuracy meets the realization that omission can be more honest than invention.

**Voice:** Careful questions and understated literal observations; humour from incongruity, not compulsive bureaucratic jokes.

**Chapter route:** V01-C04, V01-C08.

### Sadir, refuge quartermaster

New editorial supporting character; lifespan and appearances require local clock placement.

**Wants:** Keep Lilith's refuge materially viable without turning hardship into authority.

**Offers:** Knows roofs, routes, stores, and the limits of heroic promises.

**Cost or danger:** Scarcity tempts admission rules that exclude difficult needs.

**Internal conflict:** Loves the refuge but resents being taken for granted by its protectors.

**Voice:** Tactile, impatient with grand speeches during practical work; familiar teasing earned through years of repair.

**Chapter route:** V02-C13, V03-C13.

### Enoch

1 Enoch traditions and Genesis; scene motives proposed.

**Wants:** Carry testimony accurately between unequal powers.

**Offers:** Can reach hearings ordinary petitioners cannot.

**Cost or danger:** Access tempts others to demand guarantees he cannot give.

**Internal conflict:** Empathy for frightened petitioners conflicts with the harm alleged against them.

**Voice:** Measured, attentive to sequence and what he did not understand; wonder without inflated certainty.

**Chapter route:** V03-C04, V03-C05.

### Noah

Genesis flood narrative; ethical interiority proposed.

**Wants:** Preserve life through an event he cannot independently halt.

**Offers:** Organizes shelter and prolonged shared survival.

**Cost or danger:** Selection excludes lives; survival can become unwarranted moral prestige.

**Internal conflict:** Gratitude and grief remain entangled after the water retreats.

**Voice:** Practical instructions under strain; not a permanently serene spokesman for catastrophe.

**Chapter route:** V03-C07, V03-C09, V03-C10.

### Abraham

Genesis; Abram/Abraham name chronology retained.

**Wants:** Secure a future and relationship with the encountered promise.

**Offers:** Can travel, negotiate, and challenge judgement.

**Cost or danger:** Protective strategies repeatedly transfer risk to less powerful household members.

**Internal conflict:** Believes a promise matters while fearing his own choices could lose it.

**Voice:** Hospitable negotiation mixed with evasive self-justification; rhetorical patience under public pressure.

**Chapter route:** V04-C01, V04-C02, V04-C05, V04-C08, V04-C09.

### Sarah

Genesis; Sarai/Sarah change preserved.

**Wants:** Have a future that acknowledges her life already lived.

**Offers:** Brings household competence, scepticism, and a capacity to expose impossible assurances.

**Cost or danger:** Her insecurity can become domination of Hagar.

**Internal conflict:** Wants recognition and reproduces exclusion to secure it.

**Voice:** Compressed judgement, unsentimental observation, laughter with several emotional meanings.

**Chapter route:** V04-C02, V04-C04, V04-C07.

### Hagar

Genesis; independent testimony preserved.

**Wants:** Keep herself and Ishmael alive beyond the household that used and expelled her.

**Offers:** Builds an independent lineage and naming testimony.

**Cost or danger:** Hard-won caution can make every offered relation look like another trap.

**Internal conflict:** Needs aid without accepting renewed possession.

**Voice:** Direct about water, travel, and the child; theological insight begins in lived need, not lecture.

**Chapter route:** V04-C03, V04-C07.

### Joseph

Genesis; policy consequences retained.

**Wants:** Survive betrayal, use his ability, and bring his family through famine.

**Offers:** Turns interpretation and administration into large-scale provision.

**Cost or danger:** Centralized relief increases state ownership and dependence.

**Internal conflict:** Wants reunion without admitting how much he now resembles the systems that once controlled him.

**Voice:** Controlled courtesy, strategic delay, administrative precision; feeling leaks through when family interrupts the official role.

**Chapter route:** V04-C15, V04-C16.

### Moses

Exodus through Deuteronomy; portrayal proposed.

**Wants:** Lead a liberation he did not seek and leave it able to continue.

**Offers:** Can confront centralized power and organize a new community.

**Cost or danger:** Exhaustion and authority can reproduce the coercion he opposes.

**Internal conflict:** Public mission competes with reluctance, anger, and limited hearing capacity.

**Voice:** Reluctant formulation becoming forceful address; private frustration distinct from ceremonial speech.

**Chapter route:** V05-C03, V05-C04, V05-C09, V05-C10, V05-C16.

### Miriam

Exodus and Numbers; counter-record role proposed.

**Wants:** Make women's care, leadership, and losses visible inside the liberation.

**Offers:** Sustains public memory and collective courage.

**Cost or danger:** Rivalry over authority can narrow her own view of others.

**Internal conflict:** Committed to the movement while unwilling to disappear inside her brother's office.

**Voice:** Rhythmic public speech and brisk domestic directness; humour can hold shared memory without erasing fear.

**Chapter route:** V05-C02, V05-C07, V05-C14.

### Ruth

Ruth; no retrospective assimilation of origin.

**Wants:** Keep Naomi and herself alive and create a durable future.

**Offers:** Practical loyalty transforms the meaning of kinship and belonging.

**Cost or danger:** Her labour can be romanticized into an endless duty to sacrifice herself.

**Internal conflict:** Needs a secure arrangement without becoming merely the instrument of a lineage.

**Voice:** Observant, economical, attentive to how a promise changes tomorrow's work.

**Chapter route:** V06-C14.

### David

Samuel and Chronicles; distinct witnesses retained.

**Wants:** Survive, rule, and be recognized as legitimate.

**Offers:** Can exercise restraint, inspire loyalty, and consolidate institutions.

**Cost or danger:** Royal access enables domination, concealment, and failures toward his own household.

**Internal conflict:** The man who refuses a convenient killing later engineers one.

**Voice:** Quick social perception and genuine lyric capacity; charm becomes dangerous when it prevents honest refusal.

**Chapter route:** V06-C17, V06-C18, V06-C19, V06-C20.

### Bathsheba

2 Samuel; interiority editorial, not recovered historical testimony.

**Wants:** Remain a person and secure a future after royal power remakes her household.

**Offers:** Can preserve memory and navigate succession.

**Cost or danger:** Survival in court may require compromises that later admirers oversimplify.

**Internal conflict:** Rejects being reduced either to seductress or passive proof of another man's repentance.

**Voice:** Sparse, deliberate, alert to who can safely hear a sentence.

**Chapter route:** V06-C19, V06-C21.

### Solomon, king

Kings and Chronicles; never automatically the V2 Threshold trader.

**Wants:** Establish wise order and durable splendour.

**Offers:** Can hear a difficult case and organize immense work.

**Cost or danger:** Prestige accumulates labour extraction, taxation, and dynastic strain.

**Internal conflict:** Reputation for discernment competes with the experience of the people funding it.

**Voice:** Elegant comparison and confident public judgement; practical blind spots appear when the subject is his own administration.

**Chapter route:** V06-C21, V06-C22.

### Jesus

Distinct Gospel witnesses; incarnation bounded by approved cosmology.

**Wants:** Teach and enact relation without turning power into coercive rule.

**Offers:** Changes obligations through encounter, healing, teaching, and care.

**Cost or danger:** Followers can turn his language or absence into authority he did not grant them.

**Internal conflict:** Public urgency coexists with embodied fatigue, fear, and the limits witnesses can know.

**Voice:** Concrete images, questions, parables, direct rebukes, tenderness; avoid generic cosmic exposition and imported author mannerisms.

**Chapter route:** V09-C03, V09-C04, V09-C06, V09-C10, V09-C12, V09-C16, V09-C18.

### Mary Magdalene

Distinct Gospel witnesses; no invented certainty about gaps.

**Wants:** Remain faithful to what she witnessed and get it heard.

**Offers:** Carries consequential testimony through grief and disbelief.

**Cost or danger:** Others may use her witness while reducing her independent standing.

**Internal conflict:** Needs an account of absence without knowing in advance what she will encounter.

**Voice:** Immediate sensory precision, direct corrections, grief allowed to interrupt fluency.

**Chapter route:** V09-C19, V09-C21.

### Paul

Acts and epistles; attribution and chronology differences preserved.

**Wants:** Build and sustain communities around a transformed conviction.

**Offers:** Creates connections, arguments, aid routes, and durable correspondence.

**Cost or danger:** Rhetoric can outlive its context and support hierarchies in recipients' lives.

**Internal conflict:** Urgent persuasion competes with accountability for prior harm and current limits.

**Voice:** Argumentative momentum, compressed pivots, appeals to relationship; recipient voices must not become echoes.

**Chapter route:** V10-C05, V10-C07, V10-C08, V10-C12, V10-C20.

### Phoebe

Romans 16; delivery and performance details proposed.

**Wants:** Bring an argument and a network of people into a divided community's hearing.

**Offers:** Connects interpretation with named relationships and actual travel.

**Cost or danger:** Messenger prestige could narrow who gets to answer.

**Internal conflict:** Wants the letter understood without claiming every response as her own.

**Voice:** Composed and situationally exact; capable of restoring context through one well-placed question.

**Chapter route:** V10-C13.

### Onesimus

Philemon and related textual references; outcome not presumed.

**Wants:** Obtain a future beyond possession by another person.

**Offers:** Exposes the difference between an appeal and a changed condition.

**Cost or danger:** Others may use his situation to demonstrate their benevolence.

**Internal conflict:** Must assess risk under a correspondence he did not author.

**Voice:** Careful about promises, specific about conditions, neither grateful mascot nor flawless symbolic rebel.

**Chapter route:** V10-C14.

### Ione, Corinthian worker

New editorial name for poor Corinthian member.

**Wants:** Eat and belong after a day's work.

**Offers:** Makes ritual exclusion visible through ordinary bodily need.

**Cost or danger:** Exhaustion can make sustained participation costly.

**Internal conflict:** Wants community while resenting the burden of teaching it what hunger means.

**Voice:** Plain, wry among friends, precise when polite evasions appear.

**Chapter route:** V10-C10, V10-C11.

### Samira, manuscript custodian

New editorial late transmission character; no invented historical attribution.

**Wants:** Keep a contested archive usable without surrendering it to its patron.

**Offers:** Preserves terminology, copies, and independent custody.

**Cost or danger:** Care for records can conflict with the urgent safety of living custodians.

**Internal conflict:** Loves the collection but must accept that preservation cannot always mean keeping it in one place.

**Voice:** Patient explanation, dry affection for colleagues, firm refusal of false equivalence.

**Chapter route:** V11-C04, V11-C13.

### Nadia, repair coordinator

New editorial modern supporting character.

**Wants:** Make the changed world's routes and care practices actually work.

**Offers:** Turns revelations into completed repairs and accountable logistics.

**Cost or danger:** Can become impatient with grief that does not fit a schedule.

**Internal conflict:** Needs measurable progress without declaring unmeasurable loss finished.

**Voice:** Practical, companionable, capable of interrupting grandeur with a real need rather than a canned gag.

**Chapter route:** V12-C05, V12-C11, V12-C13, V12-C14.

## Factions

### Garden stewardship office

Editorial institution around Genesis and author Garden.

**Wants:** Preserve a successful enclosure and the authority to define its order.

**Offers:** Maintains provision, shelter, and a shared operating routine.

**Cost or danger:** Makes belonging conditional on compliance with imposed roles.

**Internal conflict:** Some stewards want interpretable rules; others treat questioning as system failure.

**Voice:** Assuring, procedural, offended by questions it cannot classify.

**Chapter route:** V01-C09, V02-C04, V02-C08, V02-C09.

### Lilith's refuge network

New editorial institution across the series.

**Wants:** Keep displaced people alive without buying obedience.

**Offers:** Provides routes, roofs, reciprocal care, and independent testimony.

**Cost or danger:** Scarcity strains generosity; protectors can accumulate informal power.

**Internal conflict:** Quartermasters demand workable limits while others resist any admission rule.

**Voice:** Practical familiarity, disagreement with affection, jokes tied to shared labour.

**Chapter route:** V02-C13, V03-C13, V04-C17, V05-C17, V06-C23, V07-C19, V08-C19, V09-C21, V10-C21, V11-C15, V12-C13.

### Watcher patronage circles

1 Enoch adaptation; not all angelic or divine beings.

**Wants:** Extend influence through instruction and privileged relation.

**Offers:** Offer arts and knowledge capable of improving life.

**Cost or danger:** Tie access to coercive personal obligations and unequal dependence.

**Internal conflict:** Teachers who want reciprocity clash with patrons who treat dependence as proof of gratitude.

**Voice:** Paternal assurance, technical confidence, injured generosity when challenged.

**Chapter route:** V03-C01, V03-C02, V03-C04, V03-C06.

### Egyptian grain and labour court

Editorial institutional focus within Genesis and Exodus; not all Egyptians.

**Wants:** Keep state continuity, food supply, and elite control.

**Offers:** Can coordinate storage and material distribution at scale.

**Cost or danger:** Turns emergency dependence into enduring extraction and hereditary coercion.

**Internal conflict:** Administrators pursuing survival conflict with elites prioritizing command.

**Voice:** Numbers used as arguments; polite euphemisms for burdens assigned downward.

**Chapter route:** V04-C16, V05-C01, V05-C04, V05-C05, V05-C06.

### Covenant households

Genesis family coalitions; not a homogeneous ethnic essence.

**Wants:** Secure land, descendants, protection, and continuity of promise.

**Offers:** Provide loyalty, mobility, practical care, and inherited testimony.

**Cost or danger:** Privilege lineage, status, and control of marriage or reproduction.

**Internal conflict:** Hagar, Sarah, children, servants, and patriarchs hold incompatible stakes.

**Voice:** Kinship language, negotiated promises, old jokes with long memories.

**Chapter route:** V04-C01, V04-C03, V04-C04, V04-C07, V04-C14, V04-C16.

### Wilderness assembly and service offices

Exodus-Leviticus-Numbers-Deuteronomy adaptation.

**Wants:** Make collective freedom livable after escape.

**Offers:** Creates distribution, courts, sanctuary work, and shared expectations.

**Cost or danger:** Rules can harden into unequal status and immune leadership.

**Internal conflict:** Caregivers, daughters, artisans, priests, and commanders dispute what freedom requires.

**Voice:** Public exhortation contrasted with informal queues, workshops, and households.

**Chapter route:** V05-C08, V05-C09, V05-C10, V05-C11, V05-C13, V05-C14, V05-C15.

### Royal and sanctuary establishments

Distinct kingdoms must remain historically and narratively separable.

**Wants:** Consolidate legitimacy, defence, taxation, and sacred prestige.

**Offers:** Can support infrastructure, justice, and collective memory.

**Cost or danger:** Extract labour, suppress complaint, and conflate divine favour with success.

**Internal conflict:** Prophets, court workers, relatives, debtors, and soldiers contest royal conduct.

**Voice:** Polished confidence at the centre; sharply different registers among those doing its work.

**Chapter route:** V06-C16, V06-C18, V06-C19, V06-C22, V07-C01, V07-C03, V07-C11.

### Dispersed testimony circles

Editorial coalition within exile and diaspora; not one historical organization.

**Wants:** Preserve continuity without intact territory or sanctuary.

**Offers:** Keeps texts, lament, practical wisdom, songs, and household stories.

**Cost or danger:** Curators may privilege respectable memory over difficult witnesses.

**Internal conflict:** Restoration advocates conflict with those who cannot or do not wish to return.

**Voice:** Many registers deliberately retained; one authorized voice would betray the institution's function.

**Chapter route:** V07-C14, V07-C16, V07-C18, V07-C19, V08-C01, V08-C04.

### Early assembly networks

Acts and epistles; local communities remain distinct.

**Wants:** Sustain witness, belonging, and aid across distance.

**Offers:** Creates hospitality, collections, teaching, and relations beyond some inherited boundaries.

**Cost or danger:** Charisma, wealth, household status, and office can become domination.

**Internal conflict:** Recipients answer messengers; poor members challenge meals; hosts contest controlling leaders.

**Voice:** Argument, personal greeting, correction, friendship, and exasperation; no universal church voice.

**Chapter route:** V10-C01, V10-C03, V10-C07, V10-C10, V10-C14, V10-C18.

### Exclusive archive patronages

Composite editorial antagonistic institution, not a whole religion.

**Wants:** Maintain legitimacy through control of surviving testimony.

**Offers:** Funds preservation, buildings, copies, and specialist labour.

**Cost or danger:** Makes access and survival conditional on doctrinal assimilation.

**Internal conflict:** Custodians wanting accurate records resist benefactors seeking unanimous ancestry.

**Voice:** Generous public language with increasingly specific private exceptions.

**Chapter route:** V08-C19, V11-C02, V11-C03, V11-C13, V11-C15.

### Firstborn preservation hierarchy

Author source institution; membership and capacity conflict unresolved.

**Wants:** Keep its assigned order continuous and its own offices necessary.

**Offers:** Maintains some routes and structures on which others depend.

**Cost or danger:** Treats controlled history and institutional survival as justification for coercive preservation.

**Internal conflict:** Existing dissent versus capacity to change must be settled by source reconciliation; not assumed.

**Voice:** Formal mandate language; panic appears as procedural escalation.

**Chapter route:** V01-C09, V12-C08.

### Recovery coalition

V2 seeds plus original cross-tradition composition.

**Wants:** Investigate shared crises without surrendering distinct histories and agency.

**Offers:** Combines otherwise unavailable maps, practices, evidence, and practical care.

**Cost or danger:** Coordination can centralize authority or turn traditions into useful accessories.

**Internal conflict:** Members differ on risk, translation, hospitality, timing, and the meaning of repair.

**Voice:** Natural camaraderie among people who disagree; vocabulary remains character-specific.

**Chapter route:** V11-C05, V11-C06, V11-C07, V11-C08, V11-C09, V11-C10, V11-C11, V11-C12, V12-C05, V12-C11.

### Thorne's continuity enterprise

Editorial development of V2 antagonist.

**Wants:** Secure private immortality and control of loss.

**Offers:** Mobilizes wealth, facilities, and technical competence.

**Cost or danger:** Transfers bodily and cognitive risk onto dependent people.

**Internal conflict:** Some workers want legitimate care; leaders frame exit as betrayal.

**Voice:** Reassuring service language concealing whose continuity receives priority.

**Chapter route:** V12-C03, V12-C07.

### The Architect's builders

V2-derived proposal; Eve linkage not automatic historical truth.

**Wants:** Break a coercive order and make another future possible.

**Offers:** Understands structural failures the official keepers deny.

**Cost or danger:** A remedy can make existing people expendable to an imagined liberation.

**Internal conflict:** Members divide over total erasure, bounded change, and accountability after intervention.

**Voice:** Exact diagnoses, impatience with platitude, internal arguments about means.

**Chapter route:** V12-C09, V12-C11, V12-C13.

# Source coverage and historical context

The outline gives all 66 books in the baseline tracking set explicit chapter destinations. This is a planning result. It does not mean that all their passages, laws, poems, visions, or letters have been rewritten. The larger source catalogue remains a separate denominator, including different biblical canons and texts beyond them.

A broad locator such as “Job 1–42” names the work under discussion; it does not certify that one chapter has adapted every speech. Scene-by-scene reading and comparison remain required. Only passage inspections explicitly recorded by the source lane count as inspected.
