# The Good Book atlas

These three editable SVG maps are **editorial proposals** around the approved Omnoid frame and twelve-volume plan. Text remains editable; each file has an accessible title and description and uses no external images or fonts.

1. [The Omnoid and the names of passage](/codex-apockalypsis/maps/01_omnoid_topology.svg) separates realm geography, gate functions, cultivation vocabularies and HALO. Its containment is conceptual. It does not claim a scientific embedding, measured distances or guaranteed routes.
2. [Historical places and changing routes](/codex-apockalypsis/maps/02_historical_geography.svg) uses coarse editorial locators for twelve places in the eastern Mediterranean and Mesopotamia. The grid shows approximate relative positions. It does not certify ancient footprints or an Exodus itinerary. Every route is dashed and labelled by its era and evidential status. Global comparison windows retain the wider scope without inventing lines of diffusion.
3. [One history is not one clock](/codex-apockalypsis/maps/03_multitrack_chronology.svg) gives twelve equal-width **reading-order** columns and five distinct tracks. Equal widths do not imply equal historical durations. The realm and personal tracks explicitly remain unestablished.

The complete accessible table equivalents are in [world reference](/codex-apockalypsis/library/reference-world-world-reference) and [chronology](/codex-apockalypsis/library/reference-world-chronology); machine-readable place, route, identity and event records are in [world.json](/codex-apockalypsis/files/world.json).

## Historical evidence and limits

The [Metropolitan Museum’s ancient Near East teaching resource](https://www.metmuseum.org/ko/-/media/files/learn/for-educators/publications-for-educators/art-of-the-ancient-near-east.pdf) supports regional geographic context. The map’s coordinates are coarse editorial values, not claimed measured data. An attempted Pleiades gazetteer check returned a bot challenge; no challenge was bypassed and no coordinate verification is claimed.

The [USCCB historical introduction](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/historicalintroduction/0), [IAA timeline](https://www.deadseascrolls.org.il/learn-about-the-scrolls/historical-timeline), [Ezra 3 note](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/ezra/3) and [Met Cyrus Cylinder reference](https://www.metmuseum.org/exhibitions/listings/2013/cyrus-cylinder) support the bounded chronological context used in the legends. The 587/586 BCE discrepancy is preserved.

## Editing and reuse

Edit the SVG directly for illustration changes. The generator in the world specification reservation rebuilds the candidate data, tables and original maps; running it will replace these lane-owned generated files, so preserve any hand-edited edition first. Preview PNGs are derived from the SVGs and are not the editable originals. No source manuscript is changed.

Visual QA records are separate from JSON/XML checks. A valid SVG file is not, by itself, visual sign-off.

volumes.title: Before the Word
volumes.summary: Before anyone can call a world good, someone has to live in it. Mother and FirstFlame face the difficulty of making company that can disagree with them. Their children inherit an unfinished creation, unequal knowledge, and the temptation to mistake making a thing for owning it.

volumes.title: The Garden and the Refusal
volumes.summary: A garden offers food, safety, and an answer to every question except who agreed to the arrangement. Lilith refuses an assigned place. Adam and Eve confront knowledge, dependence, and the cost of leaving. Beyond the gates, the first families discover that suffering does not automatically make people kinder.

volumes.title: The Waters and the Scattering
volumes.summary: Knowledge arrives with patrons attached. Enoch enters a dispute whose witnesses do not share a clock. Flood survivors preserve more than life: they preserve evidence, guilt, and the habits that made the catastrophe possible. A great building project promises reunion and creates a new argument over whose language counts.

volumes.title: The Houses of Covenant
volumes.summary: The promise of a future passes through tents, wombs, wells, bargains, and graves. Abraham's household grows into competing histories told by people with unequal power. Hagar and Sarah have different reasons to fear the same promise. Joseph eventually learns that feeding a nation can save his family while building the machinery that will later confine it.

volumes.title: The Bondage and the Liberation
volumes.summary: A river, a basket, and a fugitive begin a liberation that will outgrow all three. Leaving Egypt ends one form of bondage and exposes the difficulty of living together without its machinery. The wilderness becomes a place of food queues, sanctuary disputes, failed leadership, and arguments over the terms of freedom.

volumes.title: The Land and the Crowns
volumes.summary: The land is already inhabited. Conquest accounts, local memories, marriage bargains, and rescue stories collide before the demand for a king turns them into a national story. Ruth seeks a future in the margins. Saul and David discover what a crown can license; Solomon builds a magnificent answer to questions he cannot settle.

volumes.title: The Kingdoms and the Exile
volumes.summary: The kingdom breaks along the lines its monuments concealed. Prophets, debtors, courtiers, and displaced families argue over what is happening while empires collect payment. When the sanctuary falls, grief becomes a struggle over memory: whether to confess, accuse, endure, or refuse the explanations offered by survivors with authority.

volumes.title: The Return and the Hidden Years
volumes.summary: Return does not mean everyone comes home to the same place. Builders, displaced spouses, court survivors, healers, and insurgents attempt different forms of continuity. Esther, Judith, and Tobit belong to different kinds of telling, and their differences remain visible. Resistance hardens into institutions as new empires arrive.

volumes.title: The Word in Flesh
volumes.summary: Into a landscape already full of saviours, creditors, priests, soldiers, and exhausted families comes a life that refuses to stay in the category assigned to it. Teaching and healing change daily obligations before they provoke public crisis. The execution leaves actual wounds. What follows reaches the reader through witnesses whose differences matter.

volumes.title: The Witnesses and the Empires
volumes.summary: The story continues in kitchens, prisons, workshops, argument, and post. Acts and the letters become events happening to particular people rather than an uninterrupted speech from above. A collection can keep a distant household alive; a sentence can also protect a hierarchy. The recipients get to answer back.

volumes.title: The Unveilings and the Inheritances
volumes.summary: The end of one book becomes the beginning of its custody. Visions survive copying, translation, institutional conflict, destruction, and care. The wider religious weave becomes causally active through custodians who contribute different disciplines of remembrance, accountability, hospitality, and refusal. Their sources remain distinct even when the fictional history intersects.

volumes.title: The Return of Names
volumes.summary: Modern lives encounter records that know more names than any one witness can bear. Selected material from The Unraveling returns through a disciplined reconstruction of identity and consequence. Remembering does not make anyone entitled to another person. The final work is practical: living together after revelation, recording what changed, and repairing what cannot simply be undone.
